LESSON: CITIZENSHIP IN KENYA

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade five
Subject: General
Strand: Political Systems and Governance
Topic 4.3: Citizenship in Kenya
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Citizenship in Kenya, part of Political Systems and Governance in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade five General.

Key inquiry question: How can we promote responsible citizenship?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. discuss with peers ways of becoming a Kenyan citizen, learners with speech difficulties could use alternative modes of communication during the discussion,

2. use digital resources to find out ways of becoming a Kenyan

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. discuss with peers ways of becoming a Kenyan citizen, learners with speech difficulties could use alternative modes of communication during the discussion,
2. use digital resources to find out ways of becoming a Kenyan

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Citizenship in Kenya together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self-efficacy: Learners practise self-drive as they discuss in groups, ways in which one may lose Kenyan citizenship

and present in class.

● Citizenship: Learners develop intergroup communication skills for promotion of peaceful coexistence as they develop

communication messages on good citizenship and share with others in school.

Values

● Social Justice: Learners enhance democracy as they create and recite poems on Kenyan citizenship.

● Integrity: Learners display self-discipline as they write an essay on what may happen if one lost Kenyan citizenship.
